column1: # Colour mapping wheel, version 0.3.
# Every tile, where it is, and nothing else. This file is the wheel.
# **The wheel's version is not the mapping version.** The key stamps say which
# colour rule drew a mark and are integers, 0 through 3. This is the version of
# the tricolour arrangement -- which three squares stand for which stretch of
# the draw -- and it moves when a tile moves. Version 3 of the colour rule and
# version 0.3 of the wheel are different numbers about different things that
# happen to have arrived together.
# **One file, and all 165 in it.** `hand.tsv` held only what had been argued
# about -- the ring, the handful moved between tiers, and the rejected set --
# and the other 34 were placed by the packer falling through to its default.
# Nothing was lost that way, because the packing is deterministic and the wheel
# redrew identically. But the file did not *say* where a third of the tiles
# were, so it could not be read as the record of what was decided, and
# `purple purple white` sat in a tier with its argument written down in
# `perceptual.py` and no line here at all. Every tile now has a line.
# **The number is the position, and the position is clockwise from the top.**
# It was the triple's index in the palette enumeration, which no render could
# move -- the right choice while the ring was still being settled, when a note
# saying "promote #143" had to still mean that by the time the next picture
# came back. The ring is closed now, 360 of 360 with nothing spare, so the
# churn that protected against cannot happen, and a number is free to do the
# more useful job of telling you where to look. The ring is 1 to 63 and walks
# the hue circle; the tiers behind it follow, outward-in and clockwise within
# each; then the three sunk bands in the order they are drawn; then the six
# that average to a neutral and have no place at all.
# **The triple is on the line, so the number does not have to be trusted.**
# Keying by number alone was what stopped a triple being transcribed onto the
# wrong tile, and that protection is kept by carrying both: the engine reads
# the names, and the number is checked against the line it sits on. If the two
# disagree the file says so rather than drawing something wrong.
# To move a tile, change its angle. To renumber after moving one, sort.
#   ring <deg>    on the ring, at that angle
#   tier          off the ring, wherever the packing puts it
#   eject         off the ring by decision rather than for want of room
#   in / out <k>  off the ring, k tiers deeper / further out than that
#   sink <deg>    rejected outright; the band is read off the colour
#   hueless       averages to a neutral, so there is no hue to stand on
#  n
